app.name: Shopify (Dev Dashboard app for Shopify Admin API)

verdict.summary: Creating your own Shopify app and connecting your own dev store is self-serve and quick. Going public on the Shopify App Store adds a listing review, a protected customer data review and a one-time registration fee, which is where the real delay sits.
verdict.hands_on_effort: About 2-4 hours for Gates 1 and 2 (estimate). Public listing work is roughly 1-3 days of active effort, plus provider review (estimate).
verdict.time_to_first_connection: About 30-60 minutes once a Partner account and a development store exist (estimate).
verdict.approval_wait: None for dev-store or single-store use. Public App Store review is reported at 5-10 business days to 1-2 weeks per cycle by community sources; official timing is not published, and protected customer data review timing is not stated.

gates.name: Development app (your own account)
gates.unlocks: Create the app in the Dev Dashboard, register the Composio redirect URI, and connect your own development store through the OAuth flow.
limits: Partner staff need the Build and manage apps permission to create apps (f5).
Community reports say the Create App button stays disabled until a dev store or Partner organization exists (f7, not official).
gates.time_to_reach: Minutes to about an hour after a Partner account and a development store exist.

gates.name: Custom distribution (single store, Plus organization, or development stores)
gates.unlocks: Install the app on specific stores you control, or on development stores, without Shopify app review.
limits: Distribution method cannot be changed after selection (f49).
Custom apps cannot charge merchants through Shopify's app billing system (f51).
An organization is limited to 250 development stores; deleting one is permanent (f52).
Development stores are for testing only and are always password protected (f53, f55).
Apps installed only on development stores do not need a protected customer data review request (f23).
Access tokens: expiring offline tokens last 1 hour; online tokens last 24 hours (f13, f16).
gates.time_to_reach: Same day once a development store exists. No Shopify approval step is documented for custom distribution.

gates.name: Public distribution (Shopify App Store)
gates.unlocks: Install by any merchant through the Shopify App Store listing.
limits: Requires registering for the Shopify App Store, which has a one-time fee (amount not verified) (f50).
Shopify App Review can reject an app at its discretion (f38).
Protected customer data needs review for public apps at both level 1 and level 2 (f22).
Public apps must use expiring offline tokens for GraphQL Admin API requests by January 1, 2027 (f17).
Must be built exclusively on the GraphQL Admin API (f27).
gates.time_to_reach: Reported at about 5-10 business days to 1-2 weeks per review cycle (community sources). Official timing is not published. Protected customer data review adds time that is not quantified.

steps.title: Create or sign in to a Shopify Partner account
steps.detail: Go to partners.shopify.com and sign up or sign in. The sign-up page is reachable without a login wall. A Partner account, or a merchant store with developer permissions, is the stated prerequisite for building apps.
gotchas: Partner staff need the Build and manage apps permission to create apps. A separate Development stores permission is needed to create dev stores (f5).

steps.title: Create a development store
steps.detail: In the Partner Dashboard, create a development store to install and test the app. Dev stores are for testing only and cannot process real transactions. They are always password protected, and their myshopify.com URL cannot be changed after creation.
gotchas: Community reports say the Create App button stays disabled on a new Partner account until a dev store or Partner organization exists (f7, not official).
Organizations are limited to 250 dev stores; deleting one is permanent (f52).

steps.title: Create the app in the Dev Dashboard
steps.detail: Open the Dev Dashboard and create a new app. The Dev Dashboard replaces the Partner Dashboard for app development, while app pricing is still managed in the Partner Dashboard. Exact menu labels were not captured, so follow the on-screen 'create app' flow.
gotchas: Confirm the app shows under the same Partner organization as your development store, so you can install it there at no charge (f54).

steps.title: Copy the client ID and client secret
steps.detail: Open the app's Settings and find the Credentials section. Copy the client ID and client secret. Treat the client secret like a password and do not commit it to source control.

values.label: Client ID
values.value: from Settings > Credentials in the Dev Dashboard

values.label: Client secret
values.value: from Settings > Credentials in the Dev Dashboard

gotchas: Rotating the client secret invalidates access tokens tied to the old secret, and every store's token must then be refreshed (f18).

steps.title: Register the redirect URI
steps.detail: In the app's Settings in the Dev Dashboard, add the callback URL to the allowed redirect URIs. The redirect_uri sent during authorization must match one of these exactly, or the flow breaks. Paste the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Any mismatch in the redirect URI breaks the flow (f10).
Composio's documented default redirect URI and the one observed in its authorize probe differ. Confirm the exact value in your Composio auth config before saving (see open questions).

steps.title: Trim the scopes to what the app actually uses
steps.detail: Compare Composio's default Shopify scope list against the Admin API calls your agent actually makes. Keep only those scopes, and list the reason for each. Scopes are sent as a comma-separated list in the authorize request. Move scopes that not every merchant needs into optional scopes.
gotchas: Reviewers check scope necessity. Composio's default list is broad and should not be shipped unchanged (f25, f26).
Some scopes unlock protected customer data and add review requirements (f11).

steps.title: Create the OAUTH2 auth config in Composio
steps.detail: In Composio, create an OAUTH2 auth config for the shopify toolkit. Enter your client ID and client secret. Composio has no managed OAuth for Shopify, so you must supply your own app credentials. The authorize and token URLs are per store and use a subdomain placeholder.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Composio's S2S_OAUTH2 mode has no defaults. Use the OAUTH2 mode for the per-store flow.

steps.title: Connect your own development store and run a test authorization
steps.detail: Start the connection in Composio for your dev store's subdomain and approve the requested scopes. Then make one Admin API call to confirm the token works.
gotchas: Expiring offline tokens last 1 hour and come with a refresh token that lasts 90 days when issued (f13, f14).
Refresh tokens rotate. The old one stays usable until the new one is used, 30 days after first use, or the 90-day expiry, whichever comes first (f15).
Online tokens last 24 hours and are tied to the staff member who approved them (f16).

steps.title: Confirm the install flow and distribution choice
steps.detail: Choose custom distribution if the app only needs to run on stores you control. Read the distribution page before you select it, because the choice cannot be changed later. Installs must start from a Shopify-owned surface, not a manual myshopify.com URL entry.

values.label: Distribution
values.value: Custom distribution for dev/single-store use; Public distribution only for App Store listing

gotchas: You cannot change the distribution method after selecting it (f49).
Custom apps cannot charge merchants through Shopify's app billing system (f51).
Your app must not ask merchants to type a myshopify.com URL or domain during installation (f28).

steps.title: Draft the review materials
steps.detail: Draft the privacy policy, a scope justification for each requested scope, the testing instructions with test account credentials, and the listing copy. The App Store listing requires a privacy policy, and the testing instructions must include working credentials that stay current.
gotchas: Reviewers need test account credentials in the testing instructions, and they must be kept current (f32).
Use a demo store that is free to use. A reviewer was once stuck behind a paywall and the app was rejected (f43).

steps.title: Request protected customer data access
steps.detail: In the Partner Dashboard, open the app under Apps, go to API access requests, and request Protected customer data access. Give a reason for each protected field, including name, address, email and phone, each requested individually. Complete the Data protection details, then submit. Shopify approves only the minimum your app needs.
gotchas: Public apps need review at level 1 and level 2 (f22). Apps that use name, address, phone or email must meet both levels (f59).
A data protection review can follow and asks for evidence of data practices (f24).
Shopify says reviews focus on apps with many merchant installs, many customer records, more approved fields, and long retention (f60).

steps.title: Prepare listing assets and the store-side requirements
steps.detail: Prepare the 1200 x 1200 px app icon, feature images at 1600 x 900 px (16:9), and a demo screencast that shows setup and features as listed. Add an emergency developer contact in the Partner account. Confirm the app serves a valid TLS certificate and that app charges go only through Shopify App Pricing or the Billing API.
gotchas: Public apps must be built exclusively on the GraphQL Admin API. The REST Admin API is legacy (f27).
Apps must charge only through Shopify App Pricing or the Shopify Billing API (f29).
Missing or broken install or demo links are a reported cause of review delay (f42, community).

steps.title: Pay the App Store registration fee and submit for review
steps.detail: Register for the Shopify App Store, pay the one-time fee, and submit the app for review. Check that every requested scope has a written justification, because overreach without justification is a reported rejection cause.
gotchas: The fee amount was not verified. Check the current amount before budgeting (see open questions).
Shopify App Review can reject an app at its discretion, and requirements can change (f38).
Requesting overly broad or unnecessary scopes without justification is a reported rejection cause (f41, community).

steps.title: Wait for review and plan the token refresh
steps.detail: Wait for Shopify's review and respond to any requests in the Partner Dashboard. Meanwhile, make sure the integration refreshes expiring offline tokens, because public apps must use them for GraphQL Admin API requests by January 1, 2027.

values.label: Deadline
values.value: January 1, 2027 for expiring offline tokens on GraphQL Admin API requests (public apps)

gotchas: Community sources report 5-10 business days per review, and 1-2 weeks per cycle. Official timing is not published (f39, f40).
Requests for unapproved protected data do not fail with an HTTP error. GraphQL returns 200 with redacted fields and an errors entry (f62).

requirements.detail: Composio has no managed OAuth for Shopify. You must create the app in the Dev Dashboard and supply its client ID and secret.
The redirect_uri must exactly match a redirect URI configured in the Dev Dashboard or shopify.app.toml. Any mismatch breaks the flow.

requirements.item: State nonce check and HMAC verification on callback
requirements.detail: If you handle the callback yourself, compare the state parameter to the stored nonce and verify the HMAC. Composio's callback handles these when you use its auth config. Confirm this before relying on it.
Public apps need review for protected customer data at level 1, and at level 2 if name, address, phone or email are used. Requests go through the Partner Dashboard.

requirements.item: No protected-data review for dev-store-only installs
requirements.detail: Apps installed only on development stores do not need a protected customer data review request. A distribution method must still be selected first.

requirements.item: Expiring offline tokens for public GraphQL apps
requirements.detail: Public apps must use expiring offline access tokens for GraphQL Admin API requests by January 1, 2027. New public apps already cannot use non-expiring tokens for those requests.
The App Store listing requires a privacy policy.
Submission requires a demo screencast and test account credentials in the testing instructions.

requirements.item: Emergency developer contact and valid TLS
requirements.detail: Add an emergency developer contact in the Partner account. The app must serve a valid TLS certificate with no errors.
App icon is 1200 x 1200 px in JPEG or PNG. Feature images are 1600 x 900 px at 16:9.
New public apps must be built exclusively on the GraphQL Admin API. The REST Admin API is legacy.
Apps must charge only through Shopify App Pricing or the Shopify Billing API.
The app must not ask merchants to type a myshopify.com URL or domain during install or configuration.
Request only the access scopes that are necessary. Use optional scopes for scopes that not every merchant needs.
Public distribution requires registering for the Shopify App Store, which has a one-time fee.

scopes.scope: Composio default list (39 scopes, e.g. read_products, write_orders, read_customers)
scopes.effect: The list is broad. Reviewers check each scope for necessity, so ship only the scopes your app uses and justify each one.

scopes.scope: Customer and order scopes (read_customers, write_customers, read_orders, write_orders)
scopes.effect: Some scopes unlock protected customer data. That adds the protected data request and review at level 1 (and level 2 if name, address, phone or email are used) for public apps.
Shopify asks you to demonstrate the need for scopes such as read_all_orders. Add it only if the app needs historical orders, and be ready to justify it.
Scopes that not every merchant needs are better declared as optional, which Shopify strongly recommends.

blockers.symptom: The Create App button is disabled on a new Partner account.
blockers.cause: Community reports say the button stays disabled until a dev store or Partner organization exists. This is not official documentation.
blockers.fix: Create a development store (or set up a Partner organization) first, then retry Create App.

blockers.symptom: Authorization fails or the callback is rejected.
blockers.cause: The redirect_uri does not exactly match a URI registered in the Dev Dashboard or shopify.app.toml.
blockers.fix: Copy the exact callback URL from your Composio auth config into the app's redirect URI settings, character for character, and re-test.

blockers.symptom: Review is delayed or rejected for scope reasons.
blockers.cause: Scopes were requested without justification, which is a reported rejection cause.
blockers.fix: Trim to the scopes the app uses, move merchant-optional scopes to optional scopes, and write a justification for each one before submission.

blockers.symptom: The reviewer cannot get past the demo store.
blockers.cause: A reviewer was stuck behind a paywall because the demo store was not free, which was reported as a rejection reason.
blockers.fix: Make the demo store and any test plan free for the reviewer, and keep the test credentials current.

blockers.symptom: Review is delayed because demo or install links are broken or missing.
blockers.cause: Missing or broken install or demo links are a reported cause of delay (community source).
blockers.fix: Test every install and demo link before submitting, and confirm the redirect URI is correct.

blockers.symptom: Connections stop working after the client secret is rotated.
blockers.cause: Rotating the client secret invalidates access tokens tied to the old secret, and each store's token must be refreshed.
blockers.fix: Update the secret in Composio and refresh tokens for every connected store.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth for Shopify, so you must register your own app in the Shopify Dev Dashboard and enter its client ID and secret in Composio's OAUTH2 auth config. Authorize and token URLs are per store, built from a subdomain placeholder. Register Composio's redirect URI in the app settings. The default scope list is broad, so trim it to what you use before any review.

open_questions: Composio redirect URI: the toolkit metadata lists https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add as the default, but the authorize probe used https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback. Confirm which exact URL your Composio auth config shows and register that one with Shopify.

Authorize-endpoint validation: a probe with an invalid client_id did not return a standard OAuth error. It ended on a 403 'verifying your connection' page behind the store login. A real Dev Dashboard client ID is needed to confirm live behavior.
PKCE: not found in the pages reviewed. Support and requirements are unverified.
Install caps or rate limits for unreviewed public apps are not documented in the pages reviewed. Only dev-store limits (250 per organization) were found.
Review states (Draft, Submitted, Paused, Reviewed, Published) come from a third-party guide, not official docs. Official review timing is not published.
Whether Composio handles token refresh and rotation automatically for Shopify is not verified. Check this before relying on it in production.
Exact scopes that a given app is allowed to keep from Composio's default list were not verified. Reviewers may ask for justification of each one.
Partner-level requirements for public submission (business verification, paid plan, org admin role) were not confirmed beyond the Partner account and the Build and manage apps permission.
Protected customer data review timing and outcome after submission are not stated in official docs.
The one-time App Store registration fee amount was not stated in the pages reviewed.
Exact Partner Dashboard and Dev Dashboard menu labels for creating a dev store and an app were not captured. Follow the on-screen flow and confirm the labels.
